policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'and let not him that eateth not judge' renders a bare connective that both readings permit: ASV routinely renders δέ as 'and', and καὶ ὁ would give the same English. No note is mapped here.
ASV 'the Lord hath power to make him stand' translates the verbal idea alike for δυνατεῖ and the periphrastic δυνατὸς ἐστιν; the two readings are indistinguishable in English.
ASV reads 'for the Lord hath power to make him stand' — κύριος, not θεὸς, which ASV would have rendered 'God'.

ASV 'One man esteemeth one day above another' renders no connective at all; both readings leave the particles (μέν, and γάρ in a contrastive enumeration) without required English surface, so the absence does not distinguish them.

ASV 14:6 moves from 'regardeth it unto the Lord' straight to 'and he that eateth'; the clause 'and he that regardeth not the day, unto the Lord he regardeth it not' is absent, excluding the RP expansion.
ASV 'Christ died and lived again' shows one connective, but a correlative καὶ...καὶ need not surface in English as 'both'; the added καὶ is not distinguished by the wording.
ASV names two verbs only, 'died and lived again'; there is no 'and rose' answering καὶ ἀνέστη.
ASV 'the judgment-seat of God' renders θεοῦ; χριστοῦ would read 'of Christ'.
The variant is Greek word order only; ASV 'And every tongue shall confess to God' follows English subject-verb order under either arrangement.
ASV opens 'So then', its regular rendering of the doubled connective ἄρα οὖν; bare ἄρα would leave only a single 'then'/'so'.

ASV 'shall give account of himself to God' has an explicit 'to God', which the base reading without τῷ θεῷ does not support; but δώσει and ἀποδώσει are alike rendered 'shall give', so the remaining two readings stand.
ASV 'nothing is unclean of itself' fits either pronoun; in Koine αὐτοῦ commonly stands for the reflexive and would be rendered the same way.
ASV opens the verse 'For if because of meat', rendering the causal γάρ; δέ would give 'But'/'And'.
ASV's 'herein' does not mark number, so neither the singular τούτῳ nor the plural τούτοις is excluded.
ASV ends at 'whereby thy brother stumbleth', and the mapped textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities add or is offended, or is weak' places the clause outside the text ASV rendered.
ASV 'The faith which thou hast, have thou to thyself' renders the relative ἣν; the RP omission yields a question ('Hast thou faith?'), which ASV does not have.
ASV ends the chapter at 'whatsoever is not of faith is sin', and the mapped textual_variant note says other authorities 'insert here 16:25-27' — the doxology is not in ASV's text at this point.
